svg.text: Sequential pipeline with a parallel branch. Two separate LangFlow flows, byte-identical prompts, each with its own file inputs. gpt-4o-mini at temperature 0, traced in Langfuse.
FLOW 1 — PRD Genie · Human in the Loop

Agent 2 was given an empty extraction and correctly
refused. Agent 3 then read that refusal and wrote user
stories from it, inventing a login system nobody had
mentioned. Agent 5 sized those invented stories and
Agent 4 assigned owners to their gaps.
Agent 2 did everything right and the system still
produced a fabricated product. A refusal is only as
strong as the next agent's willingness to notice one.
Agent 1 needs no check — its input is the file itself.
Every run traced: resolved prompt, tokens in and out,
did the output assert what the source did not say?
did what the source did say fail to reach the output?
does it claim the source was more complete than it was?
Grounding measures invention; Coverage measures omission.
Omission is more than twice as common as invention — in a system
every rule of which was written to prevent invention.
A judge may score 0 only if it can quote the offending line.
1 · The two flows are separate LangFlow flows, each holding its own file nodes and its own Prompt Template node — the source document and the template are loaded
twice, once per flow. Nothing is shared between them except the prompt text, which is kept byte-identical, so that any difference in output is attributable to the
checkpoint and to nothing else. The Prompt Template node merges the extraction with the template file; that merged text is what Agent 2 receives.
2 · Why a sequential pipeline: the order is fixed by dependency, not judgement. Stories need requirements, gaps need stories, sizing needs something to size. An
orchestrator would spend an LLM call deciding the same thing every run; a router needs varied request types, which this does not have.
3 · The supplied PRD template was amended twice. Its Priority column offered no "Not stated" option, so every requirement came back "Must". Its non-functional table
carried placeholder rows pre-filled with "Performance" and "Security", which appeared verbatim in generated PRDs — two prompt revisions had been spent telling
Agent 2 not to do what its own input was demonstrating. Both originals are kept in the repository for comparison.
4 · Agents 4 and 5 run in parallel and never see each other's output, so they can disagree — one marking a story blocked while the other sizes it confidently. This is
deliberate. Two independent readings of the same stories cross-check each other, and a disagreement is a signal that one of them is wrong. Chaining them would
remove the contradiction by making Agent 5 inherit Agent 4's judgement — quieter output, less information. Nothing currently reconciles the two, which is the cost.
5 · Known limitation: the extractor was tuned on meeting transcripts. On a structured product brief it loses header fields and labelled sections, because its output
schema has no place to put them. Diagnosed, not fixed.
